liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Audience recording conveys how much fun everyone present was having during this song [13]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Singled out as exceptional, along with Terrapin [14]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Reviewer hears an oily, funky, slinky version, not yet fully developed, with the band probing for grooves and Brent strong [19]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Singled out as an excellent version, one Phil fans will especially enjoy [8]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Attendee singles out Terrapin as nice, along with Shakedown [18]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Named among the excellent versions and highlights of the show [8]
- **Playin' in the Barn"** (1 review): Reviewer thinks this analog-tape source may include the odd 'Playing In The Barn' lyrics [10]
- **Take A Step Back 1** (1 review): Reviewer notes Jerry plays Cornell's alma mater during the first one [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-05-07.fob.sonyecm999.morris.100242.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 24 songs; 182 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape flips occur in Bertha, spliced with Soundforge, and between Drums and Space [1]
- **gd1980-05-07.128832.naks.mason.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 155 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1980-05-07.152802.senn.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 156 min [3]
- **gd80-05-07.sbd.miller.26349.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 4.12/5 by 16 [5]
- **gd80-05-07.naks.clugston.3294.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 154 min; rated 3.86/5 by 14 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has warm ambience that puts the listener in the dim, smoky room; Audience source lacks hi-fi soundboard sound but captures the atmosphere of being there; Audience recording has harsh cuts between Shakedown and Bertha, and between Playin and Good Lovin' [8][13][16]

## Around the show

- Attendee says it was the last indoor general admission concert they attended; vocals by Bob, Jerry and Brent were incredible [18]
- Attendee prefers this show to Cornell 77, finding 77 vocals have too much reverb and effects [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-05-07.fob.sonyecm999.morris.100242.flac16**: taped by Bob Morris; source: (fob) Sony Ecm-990 Stereo Mic > Cassette Master (marantz Superscope Cd320 maxell Udxlii); [1]
- **gd1980-05-07.128832.naks.mason.flac16**: taped by Mason B. Taylor; source: Recorded By Mason Taylor on a Nakamichi 550 Cassette Deck, on chrome tapes, with Nakamichi microphones [2]. Also: Taper Mason B. Taylor of Chicago used Nakamichi 550 deck with Nakamichi 300 shotgun-capsule mics on earlier recordings [2]
- **gd1980-05-07.152802.senn.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Recorded, Transferred and Mastered by Rob Eaton; transferred by Mastered by Scott Clugston April 2021; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; (2)Sennheiser 441 mics (Left + Right) + (1) Sennheiser 421 mic (Center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [3]. Also: Master from Rob Eaton, coordinated by Charlie Miller; Nakamichi 700 and 300 blend patches Bertha and Drums [3]
- **gd80-05-07.sbd.miller.26349.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]. Also: Soundboard lineage: cassette master to reel to DAT to CD to EAC to SHN, converted by Charlie Miller [5]
- **gd80-05-07.naks.clugston.3294.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Nakamichi CM700 + Nakamichi CM300 blend [6]. Also: Reviewer points to an etree soundboard source of this show, in place of the audience tape [17]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [Grateful Dead Poster 1980-05-07 - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/grateful-dead-poster-1980-05-07-07/) [21]
- Poster by Peter Simon Grateful Dead: [1980-05-07 Barton Hall, Cornell U., Ithaca, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1980-05-07-barton-hall-cornell-u-ithaca-ny-usa/) [22]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1980-05-07 Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1980-05-07-ticket/) [23]
